en: The Kauśika Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Thus have I heard.

At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain together with a great community of monks and many hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas, all of whom were in the state of youth.
There, the Blessed One addressed Śakra, the lord of the gods.
This, Kauśika, is the meaning of the perfection of wisdom: the perfection of wisdom is not to be viewed as dual, nor as non-dual;
not from the perspective of signs, nor from the perspective of signlessness;
not through accumulation, nor through non-accumulation.
Neither by way of addition nor by way of subtraction;
neither by way of affliction nor by way of non-affliction;
neither by way of purification nor by way of non-purification.
Neither by way of relinquishment nor by way of non-relinquishment;
neither by way of abiding nor by way of non-abiding;
neither by way of conjunction nor by way of non-conjunction.
Neither through connection nor through non-connection;
neither through conditionality nor through non-conditionality;
neither through dharma nor through non-dharma.
It is not to be known by means of suchness, nor by means of non-suchness;
not by means of the limit of reality, nor by means of the non-limit of reality.
In this very way, Kauśika, is the meaning of this perfection of wisdom:
namely, because all phenomena are equal, the perfection of wisdom is equal;
because all phenomena are secluded, the perfection of wisdom is secluded.
Because all dharmas are immovable, the perfection of wisdom is immovable;
because all dharmas are not to be conceptualized, the perfection of wisdom is non-conceptualization;
because all dharmas are fearless, the perfection of wisdom is fearless.
Because all phenomena are free from fear, the perfection of wisdom is fearless;
because all phenomena have a single flavor, the perfection of wisdom has a single flavor;
because all phenomena are non-arising, the perfection of wisdom is non-arising.
Because all phenomena are non-ceasing, the perfection of wisdom is non-ceasing;
because all phenomena are like space, the perfection of wisdom is like space;
because form is limitless, the perfection of wisdom is limitless.
Thus, because feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are infinite, the perfection of wisdom is infinite.
Because the earth element is infinite, the perfection of wisdom is infinite.
Likewise, because the water element, fire element, wind element, space element, and consciousness element are infinite, the perfection of wisdom is infinite.
Because Mount Sumeru is limitless, the perfection of wisdom is limitless;
because the oceans are limitless, the perfection of wisdom is limitless;
because it is equal to a vajra, the perfection of wisdom is equal.
Because all phenomena are non-differentiated, the perfection of wisdom is non-differentiated;
because all phenomena (in their intrinsic nature) are unapprehendable, the perfection of wisdom is unapprehendable.
Because all phenomena are equal in their non-conceptualization, the perfection of wisdom is equal in its non-conceptualization.
Because all phenomena are inactive, the perfection of wisdom is inactive;
because all phenomena are inconceivable, the perfection of wisdom is inconceivable.

In this way, because the perfection of generosity, the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of vigor, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the perfection of wisdom are limitless due to the purity of the three spheres, the perfection of wisdom is limitless.
The perfection of wisdom is said to consist of the eighteen kinds of emptiness,
namely: internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness,
the emptiness of the ultimate (paramārtha), the emptiness of the conditioned, the emptiness of the unconditioned, absolute emptiness, and the emptiness of that which has no beginning or end.

The emptiness of the aspects, the emptiness of intrinsic nature, the emptiness of specific characteristics, the emptiness of all phenomena, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of self-nature, and the emptiness of the self-nature of non-existence— this, in brief, is called the perfection of wisdom.
"A star, a visual fault, a lamp, an illusion, a dewdrop, a bubble, a dream, a flash of lightning, and a cloud—thus should the conditioned be viewed. (Kauś, Vaidya 96)
Neither ceasing nor arising, neither annihilated nor eternal,
not a unity nor a plurality, without coming and without going.
I pay homage to the Fully Awakened One, the best among speakers, who taught dependent origination— the auspicious stilling of conceptual proliferation.
Homage to all the Three Jewels—past, future, and present—in the ten directions.
Homage to the Blessed Lady Prajñāpāramitā, who is well-manifested by all Tathāgatas and is known and authorized by all Tathāgatas.
(Oṃ) Prajñe, Mahāprajñe, Prajñāvabhāse, Prajñālokakāri, Ajñānavidhamane, Siddhe, Susiddhe, Siddhyamāne.
O you who are beautiful in all your limbs, who are fond of devotion, who hold out the hand of grace, and who grant consolation: succeed, succeed!
awaken, awaken!
Tremble, tremble! Move, move!
Roar, roar!
Come, do not delay for the Blessed One; svāhā!
Homage to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharmodgata, the Greatly Compassionate One.
Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom! It is as follows:

in the dharma of the Sage, in the dharma of gathering, in the dharma of favoring, in the dharma of liberation, in the dharma of favoring sentient beings, in the dharma of Vaiśravaṇa, in the dharma of universal revolving, in the dharma of gathering through the grasping of virtues, and in the dharma that pervades everywhere.
Svāhā to the Dharma that is perfectly complete at all times!
Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom!
It is as follows: akhane nikhane mukhana nekhane (avaravandane) paṭane paṭane paṭare svāhā!
Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom! It is as follows: Gaṅgā, Gaṅgā, O Gaṅgā who illuminates the banks, Gaṅgā, svāhā!
Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom!
It is as follows: *Śrīye śrīye muni śrīye śrīyase svāhā!*
Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom!
It is as follows: Oṃ vajrabale svāhā!
Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom!
It is as follows: Oṃ hrī śrī dhī śruti smṛti mati gati vijaye svāhā!
Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom!
It is as follows: bambari bambari mahābambari būru būru mahābūru svāhā!
Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom!
It is as follows: Hūte hūte hūvitāśane sarvakarmāvaraṇane svāhā! Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom!
It is as follows: Oṃ orolik svāhā.
Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom!
It is as follows: Oṃ sarvavit svāhā!
Homage to the Perfection of Wisdom.
It is as follows: Gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā.

Thus spoke the Blessed One. The Venerable Śāriputra, Śakra the lord of the gods, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and that entire assembly— including the world of gods, gandharvas, humans, and asuras— rejoiced and highly praised what the Blessed One had spoken.
The Prajñāpāramitā named Kauśika is completed.
